To be sure, the seminormalization <MATH_0001> of <MATH_0002> is a seminormal

Moreover, for any morphism <MATH_0004> of schemes we obtain a

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. The following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is seminormal,
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0003> is equal to its own seminormalization, i.e., the morphism
<MATH_0004> is an isomorphism,
<STRUCT_0004> if <MATH_0005> is a universal homeomorphism inducing isomorphisms
on residue fields with <MATH_0006> reduced, then <MATH_0007> is an isomorphism.
<STRUCT_0005>

The equivalence of (1) and (2) is clear from
Lemma <REF_0001>. If (3) holds, then <MATH_0001>
is an isomorphism and we see that (2) holds.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Assume (2) holds and let <MATH_0002> be a universal homeomorphism
inducing isomorphisms on residue fields with <MATH_0003> reduced. Then there exists
a factorization <MATH_0004> of <MATH_0005> by
Lemma <REF_0002>. Then <MATH_0006> is a closed immersion
(by Schemes, Lemma <REF_0003>
and the fact that <MATH_0007> is separated for example by
Lemma <REF_0004>). Since <MATH_0008>
is also a bijection on points, the reducedness of <MATH_0009> shows that it
has to be an isomorphism. This finishes the proof.
